script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for February 24. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

We've sent humans to the Moon, robots to Mars, telescopes to the edge of the solar system.  Yet right here on Earth, beneath the waves, lies a world we've barely glimpsed.  The deep ocean is the last great frontier—and it's stranger than any alien planet.

We've mapped only about 20% of the ocean floor in detail. The rest remains largely unknown—dark, unexplored, full of mysteries. More people have walked on the Moon than have visited the deepest trenches. At Challenger Deep, pressure is over 1,000 times surface pressure—enough to crush a submarine.  Yet fish, shrimp, and microbes live there.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: The greatest mysteries aren't always far away.  The deep ocean reminds us that wonder exists in our own world, undiscovered.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Inner Depths - Explore What's Close.

Here's your activity: What's something close to you—a relationship, a place, a subject—that you've only explored on the surface? Commit to going deeper this week. Ask new questions, visit unexplored corners, read beyond the headlines. Depth rewards explorers. This helps you discover unexplored depths in familiar territory.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about the deep ocean mystery can be applied to inner depths - explore what's close. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
